title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir, 8 Oct to 20 Oct 2026
summary: Between 8 Oct and 20 Oct 2026 the land barely changed, while the lake went from 29.91 km2 to 28.52 km2. Both dates carry flags, so the lake change and every other number here should be read with low confidence.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: Over 12 days the lake changed by -1.39 km2, or -4.6%. Mean HV and mean HH both moved by 0.1 dB. In HV, 0.86 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 0.22 km2 darker; in HH, 0.95 km2 turned brighter and 0.29 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: Built-up land rose 0.52 dB in HV and 0.34 dB in HH. Rough dry ground and fields had 0.32 km2 brighter in HV, and trees, shrub and rugged slopes 0.24 km2. The open water type fell 0.37 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause: both dates share the same October offset, which is why the land looks steady between them; reprocessed files would show it. Possible cause for the lake: real drawdown, or a lake threshold that moved on 8 Oct; the dam's level records would tell them apart.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: 8 Oct 2026 carries two flags: the lake water threshold moved more than 1.0 dB from the previous date, and backscatter over built-up land shifted more than 0.5 dB from its June-September median. 20 Oct 2026 carries the backscatter flag too. Lake areas are approximate: 8.9% and 8.2% of the outline falls on land in the optical photo.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Do not use this pair on its own. Compare each October date with an unflagged summer date, and ask NASA whether the October products will be reprocessed.
